18Definitions and abbreviations

Definitions follow TenneT, GOPACS, the ACM and the grid operators where these publish one; the source column shows where each definition comes from. Terms marked ICM are defined for this methodology.

TermMeaningSource
ACEREuropean Union Agency for the Cooperation of Energy Regulators.ACER
aFRRAutomatic frequency restoration reserve. TenneT procures aFRR through bid obligations: BSPs are contracted to provide balancing energy bids to TenneT at certain times.TenneT
Allocation pointVirtual point at which the energy exchange between an installation and the grid is administratively assigned to a market party, as if it were measured at the transfer point of the connection.ACM
Backtest limitsRules that restrict how far the full potential may use balancing prices known only after delivery: a minimum price gap of EUR 50 per MWh, a maximum volume of 100% of rated power and no position in regulation state 2 (section 7).ICM
Balancing capacityPower, in MW, that a balancing service provider holds in reserve for TenneT for a period, such as a 4-hour block.TenneT
Balancing energy pricePrice of activated upward or downward balancing energy in a quarter-hour: the price of the highest activated aFRR bid upward, or the lowest downward, or the Incident Reserve bid where that is more extreme.TenneT
Balancing energyEnergy, in MWh, delivered upward or downward when TenneT activates balancing capacity or a balancing energy bid.TenneT
BESSBattery energy storage system.ICM
BRPBalance responsible party: responsible for maintaining the balance between demand and supply in its own portfolio, and financially responsible for imbalances in its portfolio of allocation points.TenneT
BSPBalancing service provider: helps restore system frequency by offering balancing services to TenneT; one or more assets, or a pool of smaller assets, must be prequalified.TenneT
Capture rateRealised results ÷ full potential × 100%, rounded to whole percentages (section 9).ICM
CBCCapacity limitation contract: the connected party agrees with its grid operator to limit the requested transport capacity when the grid operator requests it.GOPACS
CHPCombined heat and power unit (in Dutch: WKK): typically a gas engine that produces electricity and heat; in greenhouses also CO2 for the crops.ICM
CongestionThe situation in which the demand for transport of electricity exceeds the available transport capacity.GOPACS
Connection and transport agreementAgreement between the connected party and the grid operator for the connection and the transport of electricity; it sets the GTV and the connection category.ICM
CSCCapacity steering contract (capaciteitssturingscontract): the connected party adjusts its consumption or feed-in, down or up, at agreed times or when the grid operator requests it, against a fee; at Enexis it replaces the CBC.Enexis
D-1The day before delivery.ICM
DADay-ahead market (EPEX Spot), in which prices are set one day before delivery.ICM
Delta with expected revenuesRealised results − expected revenues, in EUR. A negative value indicates results below expected revenues.ICM
Depth of dischargeShare of the nominal capacity that may be discharged in one cycle: maximum state of charge − minimum state of charge.ICM
DowntimeTime in which the battery cannot charge or discharge because of a fault or maintenance: every quarter-hour that a fault or maintenance event in the EMS log touches (section 10).ICM
EANUnique 18-digit identification number of a connection, used among other things to exchange meter data between supplier and grid operator; each extra metering point receives its own EAN.Stedin, Enexis
EMSEnergy management system that controls the battery on site.ICM
Energy taxEnergiebelasting: tax per kWh of electricity supplied through a connection, at a rate that falls with the annual offtake, in brackets.Vattenfall
ENTSO-EEuropean Network of Transmission System Operators for Electricity, which runs the Transparency Platform.ENTSO-E
Expected revenues80% of the full potential, in EUR (section 8).ICM
FCRFrequency containment reserve: activated automatically on the basis of the system frequency rather than by the TSO; auctioned per 4-hour block.TenneT, regelleistung.net
Full potentialMaximum earnings in EUR of the same battery on the same site, with perfect foresight of auction prices, balancing prices within the backtest limits, a two-day rolling horizon, and within the limits of the site (section 7); calculated at full availability and with actual downtime.ICM
GOPACSThe tool by and for grid operators to reduce congestion on the electricity grid; a partnership of the Dutch grid operators for joint congestion management.GOPACS
GTVGecontracteerd transportvermogen (contracted transport capacity): determines how much power a large consumer may transport over the grid; the power a business expects to take at most in a given period. Contracted separately for import and export.ACM, Stedin
IDIntraday market, in which quarter-hours are traded until shortly before delivery.ICM
ID1EPEX Spot intraday price index: the volume-weighted average price of the trades in the last hour before delivery of a product.EPEX Spot
ID3EPEX Spot intraday price index: the volume-weighted average price of the trades in the last three hours before delivery.EPEX Spot
ImbalanceThe difference between the metered and the traded volumes of a BRP portfolio, settled with the BRP at the imbalance price.TenneT
Incident ReserveTenneT's manually activated reserve (mFRR), procured with energy bids since 1 September 2026, replacing the directly activated mFRR product.TenneT
ISPImbalance settlement period of 15 minutes; a BRP can correct its imbalance until the end of the ISP.TenneT
kW-maxSeparate register in the electricity meter that records the highest power taken from the grid per month; charged per kW per month.Stedin
MARIEuropean platform for the exchange of mFRR balancing energy; TenneT connected on 2 December 2025.TenneT
mFRRManual frequency restoration reserve, activated on instruction of the TSO. Since 1 September 2026, TenneT's mFRR is Incident Reserve (see there).TenneT, TenneT
MLOEAMeerdere leveranciers op één aansluiting (multiple suppliers on one connection): a connection with one or more additional allocation points, each with its own EAN, meter, supplier and BRP, while the connection agreement and GTV remain one.Systeemcode elektriciteit 2026, Enexis
MSPMetering service provider: certified company responsible for the meters of a connection and for providing their data.ICM
Nominal capacityEnergy capacity of the battery as stated on the datasheet or in the warranty, in MWh.ICM
Passive balancingA BRP deliberately takes an imbalance in its portfolio opposite to the system imbalance and receives the imbalance price for it.TenneT
Perfect foresightOptimisation with prices known in advance; an upper bound for achievable results.ICM
PICASSOEuropean platform for the exchange of aFRR balancing energy, which TenneT joined in October 2024; its cross-border price is not used in Dutch balancing energy and imbalance prices.TenneT
Price impactMovement of the balancing energy or imbalance price against the battery caused by its own volume, at α per MW (section 7).ICM
ProjectOne site with one connection agreement and one or more battery assets.ICM
Project infoSite limits used in the full potential: power, state of charge, round-trip efficiency, prequalification, warranty, GTV, and PV and consumption (section 7).ICM
Rated powerMaximum charge and discharge power of a battery, in MW.ICM
PVSolar photovoltaic installation.ICM
Realised resultsEarnings of the battery in EUR per revenue driver, from the optimizer report, net of grid costs, energy tax and degradation costs calculated from meter data, before fees (section 6).ICM
RedispatchThe grid operator reduces the demand for transport capacity using intraday or same-day bids from the market.GOPACS
Regulation stateState of TenneT's balancing in a quarter-hour: 0 no regulation, +1 upward only, −1 downward only, 2 both directions; it determines which price settles the imbalance.TenneT
Revenue driverComponent of realised results, full potential and expected revenues: day-ahead, intraday, imbalance, FCR, aFRR, mFRR, grid costs (including energy tax), degradation costs, stored energy carried and downtime.ICM
RTERound-trip efficiency: energy discharged ÷ energy charged, corrected for the change in stored energy over the period.ICM
SDACSingle day-ahead coupling: the European coupling of day-ahead markets.NEMO Committee
SDE++Stimulering Duurzame Energieproductie en Klimaattransitie: Dutch operating subsidy for renewable energy, paid per unit produced.RVO
Secondary allocation pointAn allocation point that the grid operator assigns to a connection in addition to the primary allocation point; since 2026 called an additional allocation point.ACM, Systeemcode elektriciteit 2026
SoCState of charge of the battery, as a percentage of nominal capacity.ICM
Stochastic benchmarkInternal check on the full potential: a plan made on scenarios without knowledge of the day's balancing prices, settled on the actual day (section 5).ICM
Storage capacityNominal energy capacity of a battery, in MWh, as stated on the datasheet or in the warranty.ICM
Stored energy carriedChange in stored energy over a day, valued at the average day-ahead price of the day × √RTE; a driver of its own in the full potential (section 7).ICM
TBTRTime-block bound transport right: the right to transport within time blocks agreed with the grid operator; available on regional grids.ACM
TDTRTime-duration bound transport right: the right to transport during at least 85% of the hours in a year; available on the TenneT high-voltage grid.ACM
TSOTransmission system operator; in the Netherlands, TenneT.ICM
Usable capacityNominal capacity × (maximum state of charge − minimum state of charge), in MWh.ICM
Value ladderVariants of the full potential, each adding one market or freedom: L0 day-ahead only, L1 plus capacity markets, L2 the full potential, L3 the theoretical ceiling (section 5).ICM
WbmWet belastingen op milieugrondslag: the Dutch act on environmental taxes, which includes the energy tax.Ministry of Finance
YTDYear to date.ICM

19Changes to this methodology

Every change is published with a new version number and date, and clients are informed by email. After a change, past months are recalculated under the new rules where the data allows; months that cannot be recalculated are marked as not comparable. The three most recent versions are shown first.

VersionDateChange
0.3313 Oct 2026Full potential aligned with the current model: two-day rolling horizon with the stored energy at midnight chosen together with the next day, and stored energy carried as a driver of its own, replacing the fixed midpoint at midnight; backtest limits with a maximum volume of 100% of rated power instead of 30%, within the room the connection leaves; aFRR energy without a capacity contract and the exception for restoring charge after activation; imbalance prices by regulation state; price impact on aFRR energy and imbalance; aFRR capacity in both products at the average accepted price, capped at the monthly 95th percentile; pro-rata activation and settlement of shortfall; reserves within the GTV; intraday left out until continuous intraday prices are collected, and the ID1 index no longer used. Rated power, storage capacity and prequalified MW per product added, with defaults where the intake gives none; round-trip efficiency measured over at least 7 days and corrected for the change in stored energy; downtime from EMS status events; PV, consumption and pooling specified. Checks on the model, value ladder and stochastic benchmark added to section 5; results final three months after the month. Limitations, effect on the capture rate, open questions and backlog updated; industry practice, sources and definitions added.
0.327 Oct 2026Full potential specified per decision: one day per run, per quarter-hour, in three stages by gate closure; perfect foresight on day-ahead and capacity auctions and on the ID1 intraday index; settled imbalance prices used only within a rule (EUR 50 threshold, 30% cap, no regulation state 2); FCR at most rated power ÷ 1.25 with 15 minutes of energy; aFRR per direction with energy for the whole block, and energy held for FCR and aFRR added up; mFRR left out; all assets on a connection optimised together; usable capacity from nominal capacity and state-of-charge window; measured round-trip efficiency; cycle limit plus degradation cost; grid costs on the connection peak with kWh tariff and energy tax, the bracket set from the connection meter; congestion limits applied when declared; two runs per day. Until licensed intraday data are in place, intraday and imbalance are compared together; realised mFRR revenue is left out of the capture rate. aFRR and mFRR shown as separate drivers; imbalance and balancing energy prices defined per direction; grid costs formula completed; capture rate defined on the full potential at full availability. Industry practice added to section 3 and effect on the capture rate to section 14. Correction: Dutch balancing energy and imbalance prices do not use the PICASSO cross-border price. Open questions added on capture rate and downtime, peak shaving, reduced available power, aFRR, mFRR, intraday licence, energy tax, PV subsidy and FCR; questions on the import peak and on negative full potential closed. Sources and definitions added.
0.317 Oct 2026First versions without intraday in the full potential until licensed EPEX Spot data are in place.
